> [!WARNING]
> Everything on this page is **experimental**. It may change significantly between minor versions. See [API overview and stability](/docs/api) for the exact list and the compatibility policy.

## Drag

[`MoveDragDirective`](/docs/reference/move-drag-directive) makes an element follow the pointer and settle with constraints, elastic edges, momentum, snap-to-origin or snap points. `moveWhileDrag` holds a state while the gesture is active (for example, lifting a card).

:::code draggable.ts

```ts
@Component({
  selector: 'app-draggable',
  imports: [MoveDragDirective],
  template: `
    <div moveDrag="x" [moveDragSnapToOrigin]="true" [moveWhileDrag]="{ scale: [1, 1.05] }">
      Drag
    </div>
  `,
})
export class Draggable {}
```

[View source](https://github.com/Andersseen/angular-movement/blob/main/src/docs-snippets/experimental.ts#L5-L14)

Drag depends on pointer capture, constraints measured from real layout and touch behaviour that a generic controls panel cannot represent. It has a dedicated surface: [open the drag playground](/demos/drag).

## Layout

[`MoveLayoutDirective`](/docs/reference/move-layout-directive) animates an element from where it was to where it is after a layout change, with a FLIP technique, and can share an identity between elements.

:::code reorder.ts

```ts
@Component({
  selector: 'app-reorder',
  imports: [MoveLayoutDirective],
  template: `
    @for (item of items; track item) {
      <div moveLayout>{{ item }}</div>
    }
  `,
})
export class Reorder {
  protected readonly items = ['a', 'b', 'c'];
}
```

[View source](https://github.com/Andersseen/angular-movement/blob/main/src/docs-snippets/experimental.ts#L18-L29)

Layout transitions need real DOM measurements across a re-render, so they are shown in the [layout playground](/demos/layout), not in a controls panel. The measured contract — supported geometry, interruption, shared elements, limits — is in [Layout motion](/docs/guides/layout).

## Targets and triggers

[`MoveTargetDirective`](/docs/reference/move-target-directive) plays forward while a boolean is true and reverses when it becomes false; [`MoveTriggerDirective`](/docs/reference/move-trigger-directive) resets or exposes an imperative handle. Prefer [variants](/docs/guides/variants) or [`MoveAnimator`](/docs/reference/move-animator) in stable code. See the [target playground](/demos/target).

## Smooth scroll

[`MoveSmoothScrollDirective`](/docs/reference/move-smooth-scroll-directive) and [`SmoothScrollService`](/docs/reference/smooth-scroll-service) interpolate wheel and touch input on a scroll container. They change a basic browser behaviour, so they are opt-in and this site does not enable them globally. See the [smooth-scroll playground](/demos/smooth-scroll).
